searches.note: Twenty searches of twenty eight, eight unspent; one further call was refused by the tool for two blocked news domains and is counted in the twenty. Ten were restricted to a house's own domain or a primary body (Mount Mary, Yarra Yering, Yeringberg, Coldstream Hills, Chandon twice, the Australian Dictionary of Biography twice, the Victorian Heritage Database). No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record read with one instruction, refute it: dates, people, grapes, sites, making, ageing, serving, label, story, cards and questions, then the house rules.
Edits made in place; the fragment lints sound with five records refuted.

The founder's death in 2006 against one summary's 1998: Wine Selectors and the author's Medical Journal of Australia obituary give 27 June 2006. Sound.

The making and the vineyard shares rest on the house's Quintet page, the author's reading; not searched again.

Sound, save worked at Yering, made exact.
Stables and winery of 1885 to 1891 and the plan resolved in three dimensions: the Victorian Heritage Database (H694); another entry dates the winery about 1870. Hedged.

Vines pulled out in 1921, the last vintage of the old valley: the heritage database, the house and two secondary accounts. Sound; the reason given (stronger wine) rests on one account, and the grapes before 1921 on none: cut.
Replanted in 1969 by the founder's grandson on the original north east slope; 150 years marked in 2013: the house's vineyard page and journal. Sound.

The blend (about 61 to 63 per cent Cabernet Sauvignon, a field blend), destemmed and crushed, small open tanks plunged by hand, ten to twenty one days on skins, twenty one months in French barriques about two fifths new: the house's 2022 and 2023 pages. Sound.
Yering Station's 1838: the heritage database (vines in the late 1830s), Yering Station, and the ADB (the Ryries from 1840). Hedged as Yering Station's claim.

swaps.why: Chandon Australia stands at Green Point in the Yarra, makes the wine there, and is the house behind the region record's line on traditional method sparkling wine; its Vintage Brut is the house's flagship by its own site. The record already teaches, in its appellation, sites, trap and question, that the fruit grows mostly at Whitlands and in the Strathbogie Ranges, which is the lesson a candidate needs. A swap at this point would put an unwritten, unrefuted record into a batch meant to ship whole. If the owner wants Yarra grown fruit on every page, Yering Station, with its 1838 claim, is the fallback, and the integrator may take it.

rules: No living person named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, British spelling, no dash: read across all five records after the edits. The lint's notes on firsts stand on the houses' own pages and a second account (Mount Mary's revival, Yarra Yering's 1973, Coldstream Hills' 1986 as the founder's account, the first wine at Chandon).
codexTension: The library record p-mount-mary names Dr John Middleton (dead, so allowed) and says the wines are sold largely by allocation, which is volatile, and calls the house the Yarra's benchmark, a ranking; reported, not edited.
The library's p-mount-mary Pinot Noir note says from the original plantings, and p-yarra-yering's Pinot Noir note likewise; neither was confirmed here; reported, not edited.

The region record calls the Yarra Victoria's first wine region, planted in 1838; the ADB puts the Ryrie brothers at Yering from 1840 and the heritage database says the late 1830s. Reported, not edited.
